Creates dense tracks from the columns of Parquet files

Source: R/track-import.R
gtrack.import_parquet.Rd

Creates one 'Dense' track per value column of one or more Parquet files.

Usage

gtrack.import_parquet(
  description,
  path,
  binsize,
  track.prefix = NULL,
  columns = NULL,
  defval = NaN
)

Arguments

description

a character string description

path

Parquet file path (may contain wildcards)

binsize

bin size of the newly created 'Dense' tracks (> 0)

track.prefix

prefix for the track names

columns

names of the value columns to import, or NULL for all

defval

default track value

Value

Names of the created tracks, invisibly.

Details

The files must have the interval columns 'chrom' (string), 'start' and 'end' (0-based, end exclusive; integers, or floating point numbers that are whole) and one or more value columns (integer or floating point), such as the files gextract writes with file = "x.parquet" or pandas' to_parquet. 'path' may contain wildcards, so that per-chromosome files import in one call; all the files must have the same value columns. Columns are matched by name, not by position.

'columns' selects the value columns to import, in the order of the created tracks. With 'columns = NULL' every column other than 'chrom', 'start' and 'end' is imported, and a column that is not numeric is an error.

The track of column 'col' is named '[track.prefix]col'. All the track names are checked before anything is written: a name must start with a letter and hold only letters, digits, '_' and '.' (columns are never renamed; leave such a column out with 'columns'). Existing tracks are not overwritten and no directories are created.

Values are binned as gtrack.import bins the same rows read from a tab-delimited file: each bin holds the mean of the values that overlap it, weighted by the overlap. Bases no row covers, and rows whose value is null or NaN, count as 'defval' (unless it is NaN). The rows of a chromosome may be spread over several files and row groups in any order, but may not overlap. Chromosome names are matched through the chromosome alias chain as in gtrack.import, with the same reporting of names the database does not have.

The import is all or nothing: if it fails or is interrupted, none of the tracks is created.

Supported: flat schemas; PLAIN, dictionary and BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT encodings; data pages v1 and v2; UNCOMPRESSED, SNAPPY and GZIP compression. Other compression codecs (e.g. ZSTD) and encodings (e.g. DELTA_BINARY_PACKED) are an error that names them. Unsigned integer columns are read as unsigned; decimal, date, time and timestamp columns are not numbers and are refused.

'description' is added to the created tracks as an attribute.

See also

gtrack.import_set, gtrack.import, gextract

Examples


# \donttest{
gdb.init_examples()

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
gextract("dense_track", "dense_track * 2", gintervals(1, 0, 10000), iterator = 50, file = f)
gtrack.import_parquet("from parquet", f, 50, track.prefix = "pq_", columns = "dense_track")
gextract("pq_dense_track", gintervals(1, 0, 200))
#>   chrom start end pq_dense_track intervalID
#> 1  chr1     0  50      0.1777778          1
#> 2  chr1    50 100      0.1600000          1
#> 3  chr1   100 150      0.1800000          1
#> 4  chr1   150 200      0.1600000          1
gtrack.rm("pq_dense_track", force = TRUE)
# }
